the COVID 19 lockdown did not have an impact on the incidence of hospital acquired MDR bacterial bloodstream infections or candidemia, and that the antimicrobial consumption decreased after the lockdown.
the COVID 19 lockdown was associated with increased antimicrobial consumption and no impact on incidence of candidemia and M.D.R BSI.

the COVID 19 lockdown was associated with a short term increase in antimicrobial consumption, without a change in the incidence density of hospital acquired candidaemia and multidrug resistance bacterial bloodstream infections, and without an increase in 14 and/or 30 day crude mortality.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the COVID 19 lockdown had no impact on hospital acquired candidemia or MDR BSI incidence and crude death rates.
the COVID 19 outbreak has not had a major effect on antimicrobial use and clinical outcomes.

COVID 19 has not had an impact in the incidence of MDR BSI and candidemia and in crude mortality rates, although a slight increase in antimicrobial consumption was observed in the early phase of the pandemic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antimicrobial stewardship programmes should be maintained and strengthened during the pandemic.

the COVID 19 crisis has not affected the global trend of antimicrobial consumption and hospital acquired infections, but has had a significant impact on the weekly trend of antimicrobial use, with an increase in the first six weeks after the lockdown and a subsequent reduction in the following weeks.
the COVID 19 outbreak has not had a relevant impact on antimicrobial consumption, candidemia and MRS BSI incidence, and mortality in a tertiary care centre with an active ASP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of ASPs is crucial in the fight against antimicrobial resistance.
the implementation of ASP strategies should not be delayed during the COVID 19 crisis, as they may have a positive effect on antimicrobial use, without increasing the incidence of MDR BSI.
ASP should not be interrupted during the COVID 19 pandemics, but rather adapted to the new circumstances and needs.
